punchline: A few minutes with Shannon turned into hours and a second secret.
thirty_sec: In autumn 1960 young mathematician Edward Thorp went to Claude Shannon so his blackjack paper could reach the Proceedings of the National Academy. Shannon cross-examined him, they changed the title, and then Thorp revealed his roulette idea; the talk lasted hours.
question: Which finished piece of your work should the sharpest critic see this month?
key_contrast: A checkable result, not just an idea.
